questions.q: A sprinter of mass 70 kg accelerates at 4 m/s². What force is produced?
In a third-class lever, which part is in the middle?
options: None, they are all at the ends
questions.why: Third class: F-E-R, effort between fulcrum and resistance (1-2-3 = F-R-E in the middle).

questions.q: Which forces act on a sprinter in the starting blocks?
options: Gravity, ground reaction force, air resistance
questions.why: The syllabus lists gravity, ground reaction force and air resistance.

questions.q: Draw (describe) a first-class lever and give an example from the body.
questions.model: A first-class lever has the fulcrum between the effort and the resistance: effort – fulcrum – resistance. Example: the neck when nodding the head (fulcrum is the joint between the skull and spine).
points: Fulcrum in the middle, effort and resistance at the ends
Correct body example such as the neck or triceps at the elbow
